question: The first complete census of an Indian city was conducted in ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1830**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first complete **census** conducted in an **Indian city** took place in the year **1830**.
 
• This census was conducted under the **British colonial rule**, marking the beginning of organized population surveys in India.
 
• The census focused on collecting data related to **population demographics**, including age, gender, and occupation.
 
• The city covered in the census was **Madras (now Chennai)**, a major administrative and trade hub during the colonial era.
 
• It laid the foundation for systematic data collection, which eventually evolved into the modern-day decennial census conducted by the **Registrar General of India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical context of census in India:**

 
 
• The first modern census in India was conducted in **1872** under British rule, but it was not synchronous.
 
• The first synchronous census, covering the entire country, was conducted in **1881**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the 1830 census:**
 
 
• It was among the earliest attempts at systematic population studies in India.
 
• The data collected helped in understanding the socio-economic conditions of the region and was used for **administrative planning**.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of census in India:**
 
 
• Post-independence, the **Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India** took charge of conducting censuses.
 
• The Indian Census is now conducted every **10 years**, with the latest census being planned for **2021**.
 
 
 
• **Key features of modern-day census:**
 
 
• Collects data on **demographics, literacy, employment, housing, and migration patterns**.
 
• Data is crucial for policy-making, **resource allocation**, and tracking development indicators.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The first census in Madras (1830) set a precedent for organized data collection, which became crucial during later colonial governance.
 
• The census allowed colonial administrators to assess population density, urbanization, and resources available in cities like Madras.
 
• Modern Indian census, conducted under the **Census Act of 1948**, is one of the most comprehensive data collection exercises globally.
